title.en: Currency (Denominations and Characteristics of Currency Notes) Notification 2015

completenessNote: 该法规为单篇法律文书，无分节结构；正文按官方 front 抬头逐字全录，共 2 条。

text.en:
Currency Act
(CHAPTER 69)
Currency
(Denominations and Characteristics of Currency Notes)
Notification 2015
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the currency notes issued on 11 August 2015 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

THE SCHEDULE
DESCRIPTION OF THE SINGAPORE50 (SG50) COMMEMORATIVE NOTES ISSUED ON 11 AUGUST 2015

$50
Length — 156mm
Width — 74mm
The front design features the portrait of Singapore’s first President, the late Mr Yusof bin Ishak.
The large see-through window on the left, features Singapore’s first Prime Minister, the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew. There is another see-through window that is located on the bottom right-hand corner.
Below Mr Lee’s image is a colour-switching Singapore50 (SG50) logo and a year-date that switches from ‘1965’ to ‘2015’ when the note is tilted.
The image of four children of different races and gender is depicted in the centre-left portion, and the image of the Singapore Arms is located above the words ‘THIS NOTE IS LEGAL TENDER’.
The signature and seal of Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam, Chairman, Monetary Authority of Singapore are found below the words ‘Fifty Dollars’ and the denomination numeral ‘50’.
One set of the asymmetrical serial number appears horizontal on the left-hand side while the other set appears vertical on the right-hand side.
The word ‘SINGAPORE’ is printed on the bottom centre-right portion. The Braille pattern is at the top right-hand corner.
The see-through window at the bottom right-hand corner is embossed with the denomination numeral ‘50’ in its centre, with the repetitive pattern of the denomination numeral ‘50’ at the left of that window.
The back design features two scenes showing the transformation of Singapore — on the left, a scene of Punggol New Town is depicted and on the centre-right, a scene of the National Day Parade in 1966 is depicted.
The denomination numeral ‘50’ is located at the top centre-right and at the lower centre-left of the note. The word ‘SINGAPORE’ overlaps with the denomination numeral ‘50’ at the top centre-right.
The 2 see-through windows located at the front of the note can also be seen from the back.
Predominant Colour: Gold
Secondary Colours: Brown, Blue and Red
Predominant Colour: Gold
Secondary Colours: Brown, Blue, Green and Red
$10
Length — 141mm
Width — 69mm
The front design features the portrait of Singapore’s first President, the late Mr Yusof bin Ishak.
There is a security feature on the left side, depicting the Singapore Arms, official SG50 logo, and year-dates ‘1965’ and ‘2015’, which have colour-switching effect.
The Singapore Lion symbol in gold patch with the words ‘TEN DOLLARS’ and the image of the Singapore Arms are located above the words ‘THIS NOTE IS LEGAL TENDER’. The denomination numeral ‘10’ is located at the upper-middle portion.
The signature and seal of Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam, Chairman, Monetary Authority of Singapore, are below the words ‘TEN DOLLARS’.
The security thread in the shape of Singapore island is at the lower centre of the note.
The spray of the orchid Vanda Miss Joaquim, Singapore’s national flower, is located at the centre of the note.
The word ‘SINGAPORE’ is printed on the bottom centre portion. Another Singapore Lion symbol is located at the left side of the word ‘SINGAPORE’.
The Braille pattern is at the top right-hand corner. The see-through window at the bottom right corner is embossed with the denomination numeral ‘10’ in its centre, with repetitive pattern of the denomination numeral ‘10’ at the top and bottom of that window.
Back design of the SG50 $10 Commemorative Note — ‘…regardless of race, language or religion…’
The back design features a group of eight students standing shoulder to shoulder.
The words ‘SINGAPORE Vibrant Nation, Endearing Home’ appear at the top of the note.
The denomination numeral ‘10’ is located at both the top left-hand corner and at the bottom centre-right of the note. The Singapore Lion symbol is located to the right of the denomination numeral ‘10’ and is in perfect registration with that on the front.
The see-through window located at the front of the note can also be seen from the back.
The words ‘…regardless of race, language or religion…’ are located at the bottom, to the right of the see-through window.
One set of the asymmetrical serial number appears horizontal at the bottom centre while the other set appears vertical on the right-hand side, above the Singapore Lion symbol.
Predominant Colour: Red
Secondary Colours: Brown and Pink-Purple
Predominant Colour: Red
Secondary Colour: Brown
Back design of the SG50 $10 Commemorative Note — ‘Opportunities for All’
The foreground of the back design features students learning and developing in both academic and non-academic ways.
The left side features an image of a teacher watching a group of students play soccer, while the right side depicts a teacher holding a globe, with three students in the centre.
The background depicts an engineer, a dancer, a scientist, a chef and a financial analyst, portraying the various career aspirations in different sectors of the economy.
The words ‘SINGAPORE Vibrant Nation, Endearing Home’ appear at the top of the note.
The denomination numeral ‘10’ is located at the top left-hand corner and at the bottom centre-right of the note. The Singapore Lion symbol is located to the right of the denomination numeral ‘10’ and is in perfect registration with that on the front.
The see-through window located at the front of the note can also be seen from the back. The words ‘Opportunities for All’ are located at the bottom, to the right of the see-through window.
One set of the asymmetrical serial number appears horizontal at the bottom centre while the other set appears vertical on the right-hand side, above the Singapore Lion symbol.
Back design of the SG50 $10 Commemorative Note — ‘Safe and Secure’
The back design features the Singapore Armed Forces, with personnel from the Navy, Army and Air Force depicted at the top of the note. This image is complemented by the image of the Home Team in the foreground, comprising Citizens-on-Patrol members, police officers, a paramedic and a firefighter.
The words ‘SINGAPORE Vibrant Nation, Endearing Home’ appear at the top of the note.
The denomination numeral ‘10’ is located at the top left-hand corner and at the bottom centre-right of the note. The Singapore Lion symbol is located to the right of the denomination numeral ‘10’ and is in perfect registration with that on the front.
The see-through window located at the front of the note can also be seen from the back. The words ‘Safe and Secure’ are located at the bottom, to the right of the see-through window.
One set of the asymmetrical serial number appears horizontal at the bottom centre while the other appears vertical on the right-hand side above the Singapore Lion symbol.
Back design of the SG50 $10 Commemorative Note — ‘Strong Families’
The back design features a scene of a three-generational Chinese family celebrating the wedding anniversary for the elderly couple and a newly commissioned Indian officer sharing his achievement with his parents. The scene also portrays a Malay grandfather with his grandson and a Eurasian family riding a tandem bicycle.
The words ‘SINGAPORE Vibrant Nation, Endearing Home’ appear at the top of the note.
The denomination numeral ‘10’ is located at the top left-hand corner and at the bottom centre-right of the note. The Singapore Lion symbol is located to the right of the denomination numeral ‘10’ and is in perfect registration with that on the front.
The see-through window located at the front of the note can also be seen from the back. The words ‘Strong Families’ are located at the bottom, to the right of the see-through window.
One set of the asymmetrical serial number appears horizontal at the bottom centre while the other set appears vertical on the right-hand side, above the Singapore Lion symbol.
Back design of the SG50 $10 Commemorative Note — ‘Caring Community, Active Citizenry’
The back design features a scene of community gardening, volunteers interacting with an elderly woman, and volunteers painting a flat of the less-privileged.
The words ‘SINGAPORE Vibrant Nation, Endearing Home’ appear at the top of the note.
The denomination numeral ‘10’ is located at the top left-hand corner and at the bottom centre-right of the note.
The Singapore Lion symbol is located to the right of the denomination numeral ‘10’ and is in perfect registration with that on the front.
The see-through window located at the front of the note can also be seen from the back. The words ‘Caring Community, Active Citizenry’ are located at the bottom, to the right of the see-through window.
One set of the asymmetrical serial number appears horizontal at the bottom centre, while the other set appears vertical on the right-hand side, above the Singapore Lion symbol.
